newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis gamble on Holocaust tour to Poland.
newsitem.headline: Israelis gamble on Holocaust tour to Poland.

text.p: Israel's army apologised on Thursday for the behaviour of some of its leaders-in-training reported to have gambled their nights away at Polish casinos while on an official tour of Nazi Holocaust death camps by day.
Israel Radio said nearly 60 officers at the Jewish state's School of High Command hit the hotel casinos for six nights.
It said they also played cards while on the bus to the Auschwitz-Birkenau camp where the Nazis killed at least a million of the six million Jews they systematically exterminated during World War Two.

"We are speaking of seven, eight officers and not the whole group who during the two or three nights visited casinos and that in itself testifies to poor judgment," Brigadier-General Yossi Raveh, commander of the school, told the radio.
"It's a lack of sensitivity even for a private visit and certainly when it's a visit on the part of the army and an official visit for that matter," he said.

Raveh said he was unsure whether disciplinary steps would be necessary. Overall the tour was respectable and emotional, and top officers had been moved to tears, he said. But he added further educational steps were needed.
"We must examine how we got to this situation," he said.
"It's certainly judgment we are sorry about."
